escalation.strategy: Shift from a single, long, stateful procedure to a more robust, functional, and declarative approach. Instead of micromanaging a dozen global variables across multiple steps, the skill should define two independent, self-contained "data gathering functions." Each function will be responsible for a single section of the dashboard (e.g., "Skill Performance"). It will encapsulate its own error handling and will return either a complete data object on success or a structured error object on failure. The main execution flow will then simply call these functions and assemble the final report from their results, drastically simplifying the logic and reducing the chance of state management errors.

This two-phase process, which instructs the agent to output a complete dashboard and then later "update" or "replace" it, is counter-intuitive for a generative model. escalation.strategy: **Abandon the "Render-Then-Replace" model and adopt a "Gather-Then-Render-Once" strategy.** This involves a radical simplification of the execution flow into a single, linear process. The agent will first initialize all variables with fallback values, then attempt all data gathering steps in a "best-effort" manner, and finally, render the complete dashboard exactly once at the very end. This eliminates the confusing intermediate output and the impossible "replace" instruction, aligning the skill's logic with a more natural generative process. Resilience will be achieved through clear error-handling instructions within each data-gathering step, not through a convoluted multi-phase workflow.
